audit_metadata.audit_title: Production vs Standalone Comparative Scoring & Sanity Video Audit

4_frame_and_clip_selection.stage_6d_and_6f_method: Sequential crop extraction from start of video (crops 0..25, 25..50, 50..75, 75..100)
4_frame_and_clip_selection.stage_6e_benchmark_method: Temporal anchor sampling across video timeline (ratios: 5%, 30%, 55%, 80%)
4_frame_and_clip_selection.difference_impact: On long videos with non-speaking intros (e.g. fake_001), 6D/6F captures the initial silent smiling frames (negative logits), while 6E captures active talking at 30% duration (+8.84 logit).

6_sigmoid_direction.polarity: Positive Logit -> Score > 0.50 (FAKE), Negative Logit -> Score < 0.50 (REAL)

real_001.content_analysis: Actor on phone, then turns head sharply and exits. Rapid head rotation induces 2D projection landmark deformation, triggering high temporal logits (+4.28). Baseline ViT (0.82) and GenD (0.57) also misclassified this video.

fake_001.content_analysis: Actor 01 face-swapped onto Actor 02. Frames 0-100 feature silent smiling without active speech articulation (yielding negative logits); once active speech commences around frame 200 (30% mark), LipForensics outputs +8.84 logit.

final_diagnosis.category: C) Expected model behavior on those particular video samples combined with clip sampling dynamics
final_diagnosis.explanation: Production /detect pipeline and standalone Stage 6D pipeline produce 100.00% identical outputs down to four decimal places. There is zero bug, zero polarity inversion, and zero preprocessing mismatch. The apparent paradox is explained by the fact that the two sanity samples chosen for Stage 6D are edge-case videos: real_001 exhibits rapid 2D rotation deformation (a known error mode), and fake_001 begins with 4 seconds of silent smiling before speech commences (yielding negative logits during initial silent frames). Across the full 100-video benchmark, LipForensics achieves 0.7794 AUC with 78% recall and 60% specificity.
